title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: a long computation in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' around groups attached to a pair of elements rho, sigma in a reductive group G. G appears to be GL_2-like: SG = ker det, PG = G/G_m, and T_0 is the central torus with T_0.SG = G. T_rho and T_sigma are the centralisers (tori) of rho and sigma, and N'_sigma is a normaliser-type extension of T_sigma. M_{rho,sigma} = DG^o_{rho,sigma}.SG is a semidirect product. Theta: M -> G is its projection.

On the previous page Grothendieck defined I = Ker(M -> G) and J = Ker(M -> G -> PG). He had begun to argue abstractly that J is a commutative 'radical' with toral connected components.

Here he stops ('je me complique l'existence pour être trop savant') and computes directly from the semidirect product.
- M ⊂ (T_0 × T_rho × N'_sigma).SG ≅ (T_rho × N'_sigma) × (T_0.SG) = T_rho × N'_sigma × G. Theta is pr_3 restricted to M.
- (13) M = {(x,y,f) : det f = det y = ε' det x, ε'^2 = 1}.
- Kernel to PG: f is a scalar λ, so det f = λ^2. This gives {(x,y,λ) : det y = ε det x = λ^2, ε^2 = 1}.
- Kernel to G: f = 1, which forces det y = 1 and det x = ε', so (det x)^2 = 1.

He then decides it is more natural to describe first the neutral component M^o. On the next page he gets M^o ⊂ T_rho × T_sigma × G with det x = det y = det f, and π_0 = μ_2 × μ_2. The connected kernels come out cleanly as J^o ≅ T_rho ×_{G_m} T_sigma and I^o ≅ ST_rho × ST_sigma.

Purpose: determining the structure (composition series, radical, component group) of an algebraic group of symmetries attached to solutions of the 'loop equation'. This is in the Longue Marche / Galois–Teichmüller circle of ideas.
errors: The labels on (14) are swapped relative to the definitions on the previous page (I = Ker(M->G), J = Ker(M->PG)). The set with the scalar λ ∈ G_m and det y = ε det x = λ^2 is the kernel to PG, i.e. J. The set {det y = 1, (det x)^2 = 1} is the kernel to G, i.e. I. The next page (17)-(18) uses the correct assignment for the neutral components.
In the second set, writing it inside T_rho × N'^1_sigma silently uses det y = 1. That is consistent, but the overwritten superscript is ambiguous.

ideas.what: Embedding a semidirect product M = D.SG into T_rho × N'_sigma × G via T_0.SG = G, and describing M by determinant conditions
ideas.modern_name: Elementary structure of algebraic subgroups of GL_2 × tori; computation of kernels and component groups

ideas.what: Composition series 1 ⊂ I ⊂ J ⊂ M with J a commutative 'radical', and identification of its connected part as a fibre product of tori over G_m
ideas.modern_name: Fibre product of maximal tori T_rho ×_{G_m} T_sigma; component group μ_2 × μ_2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine explicit computation of kernels and component groups of an auxiliary algebraic group. It corrects an overly abstract approach from the previous page. Nothing here seems new or significant on its own, beyond documenting the internal working of the loop-equation notes.
transcription_corrections: The condition in (13) reads ε'^2 = 1, not ε'^{12} = 1.

In (14) the first object's label was overwritten (a bold I written over something). Mathematically it is the kernel to PG (J), and the second object (written J_{ρ,x}, probably meant J_{ρ,σ}) is the kernel to G (I).
In the second set, 'N'^1_σ' is written over another symbol (the original 'N' was struck over).
